meta.archive_note: Superseded by ptc-v2-simplification.md. V2 removed tool dispatch layer, enabled bridge networking, uses pre-built role images.

feature.summary: Replace 15-tool MCP server with single ptc_execute backed by NDJSON IPC over Unix sockets, persistent Docker containers with REPL pool, host-side tool dispatch, runtime pip install, and JSONL observability.
goals: True pause-resume tool calling via Unix socket IPC
Persistent container namespaces (state survives across ptc_execute calls)
REPL pool: sub-agents share parent container (no extra pip install)
ptc_tools library usable inside container and on host

chunks.name: IPC Protocol Messages and Serialization
chunks.delivers: All IPC message types can be instantiated, serialized to NDJSON, and deserialized back with unique correlation IDs.
chunks.description: Define 8 message dataclasses (4 host-to-container, 4 container-to-host) with NDJSON encode/decode functions and UUID-based ID generators. This is the wire protocol foundation used by all IPC components.

tasks.details: ExecuteMsg(exec_id, code, type='execute'), ToolResultMsg(call_id, content, error=None, type='tool_result'), CancelMsg(exec_id, reason='timeout', type='cancel'), PingMsg(type='ping'). All use @dataclass with type field defaulted.

ToolCallMsg(call_id, tool, input: dict, type='tool_call'), CompleteMsg(exec_id, stdout, stderr='', return_code=0, namespace_keys=[], namespace_size_kb=0, type='complete'), ErrorMsg(exec_id, message, traceback='', type='error'), PongMsg(type='pong').
json.dumps(asdict(msg), separators=(',',':')) + '\n' encoded to bytes. Compact NDJSON — one message per line.
json.loads(line.strip()). Returns raw dict; caller reconstructs typed message.
new_call_id() returns f'c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}', new_exec_id() returns f'e-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}'. 12 hex chars = 48 bits of randomness.
MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE = 1_048_576 (1MB per message).
Round-trip encode/decode for each message type, ID uniqueness across 1000 calls, MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE value check. Create conftest.py with message fixture factories.

invariants.description: All 8 message types importable from ipc_protocol

verify.command: cd ~/.claude/mcp/ptc-server && python -c "from ipc_protocol import ExecuteMsg, ToolResultMsg, CancelMsg, PingMsg, ToolCallMsg, CompleteMsg, ErrorMsg, PongMsg"

cd ~/.claude/mcp/ptc-server && python -c "from ipc_protocol import *; m = ExecuteMsg('e1','print(1)'); d = decode(encode(m)); assert d['exec_id'] == 'e1' and d['code'] == 'print(1)' and d['type'] == 'execute'"

chunks.notes: Design doc Component 1, lines 260-345. Exact code provided — follow closely.

chunks.name: Code Executor with Persistent Namespace
chunks.delivers: Python code executes in a persistent namespace with stdout capture, await detection/wrapping, and tool stubs injected from an IPC client interface.
chunks.description: Build the Executor class that runs agent-written Python code inside the container. Namespace persists across calls (variables survive). Stdout/stderr captured. Top-level await detected and wrapped in async def. Tool stubs generated for each allowed tool name.

tasks.details: Init persistent _namespace dict. Store ipc_client reference. Call _setup_tool_stubs(allowed_tools).

For each tool_name: create async def _stub(_name=tool_name, **kwargs): return await self._ipc_client.call_tool(_name, kwargs). Inject into self._namespace[tool_name]. Use default arg capture to avoid closure bug.

Returns (stdout, stderr, return_code, namespace_keys, namespace_size_kb). Steps: redirect stdout/stderr to StringIO, compile(code, '<ptc>', 'exec'), detect 'await' then wrap in async def _ptc_main() + asyncio.run(), exec() in self._namespace, extract new locals, return captured output.
After each execute(), calculate approximate namespace size via sys.getsizeof. Track namespace_keys list and namespace_size_kb. Log warning at 256MB.

chunks.name: Container-side IPC Client + Runtime
chunks.delivers: A runtime process connects to a Unix socket, receives execute commands, runs code via Executor, calls tools via IPC with parallel future routing, and returns results.
chunks.description: Build IpcClient (container-side socket client with call_tool and parallel response routing) and runtime.py (REPL process entry point). Together they form the complete container-side stack.

tasks.details: connect(socket_path) via asyncio.open_unix_connection. call_tool(tool_name, params) sends ToolCallMsg, creates Future keyed by call_id, awaits Future. _response_handler() reads lines, routes ToolResultMsg to matching Future. Raise ToolError if result has error.

Parse --socket CLI arg (default repl-0.sock). Connect to /ptc_ipc/{socket_name}. Create IpcClient + Executor. Loop: read ExecuteMsg then executor.execute(code) then send CompleteMsg or ErrorMsg. Handle CancelMsg (task.cancel). Handle PingMsg (send PongMsg).

IpcClient call_tool with mock socket stream. Parallel call routing (2 concurrent call_tools, each gets correct result by call_id). ToolError raised on error result. Runtime main loop with mock socket.

chunks.name: Error Handling + Hardening + Cleanup
chunks.delivers: All error scenarios handled: crash recovery, timeouts, namespace eviction, REPL limits, pip failures, idle cleanup. Old make_kernel_code code removed.
chunks.description: Add comprehensive error handling across ipc_host, container_manager, executor, server. Remove old code: make_kernel_code from tool_implementations, old test files.

tasks.details: Container crash during exec: socket EOF, reject futures, return error, NEVER re-execute. Crash during idle: ping timeout, restart, namespace lost, warn. REPL crash: kill only that REPL, container + others survive.
Per-tool: asyncio.wait_for on dispatch. Overall: deadline timer, send CancelMsg. Max tool calls: counter, send cancel after 50.
In Executor: after each execute(), if namespace > 512MB, evict oldest non-callable objects until under 256MB.
Pip timeout: log error, container usable for stdlib. Pip failure: log package name. Docker unavailable: flag at startup, return error.
Background task: check every 60s, destroy containers with no REPLs and last_used > idle_timeout. Remove make_kernel_code from tool_implementations. Delete old test files.
Crash returns error (never re-execute). Timeout sends CancelMsg. Namespace eviction works. All errors return structured JSON.

invariants.description: Crash during execution returns error, never re-executes

All error scenarios return structured JSON errors with error key
